newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo shares backtrack as profit-taking creeps in.
newsitem.headline: Oslo shares backtrack as profit-taking creeps in.

text.p: Norwegian shares took a step backwards on Friday in line with other European bourses and as investors cashed some profits after a week of strong half-year results and general positive sentiment.
Dealers said market direction over the next two weeks would largely depend on six-month results, barring any major move in the U.S. market.
Oslo'as Total share index retreated 0.64 percent to 1,323.61 points in turnover of almost one billion crowns. The index has climbed three percent since the close last Friday.
"Today was a profit-taking day after what happened on The Street yesterday and because it is the end of a very good week," said one broker.
Drugs group Nycomed and offshore supply company Aker Maritime fell on profit taking after sharp gains a day ago when the companies' half-year results beat forecasts.
Nycomed was down three crowns at 165.50 crowns, while Aker Maritime closed two crowns down at 133 crowns.
Telecommunications group Nera fell 1.52 percent to 45.50 crowns partly on profit-taking and partly after a large U.S. investment bank downgraded the stock, dealers said.
